question: If the length of a resistor is doubled, what happens to its resistance, assuming all other factors remain constant?
solution:
The correct answer is __The resistance is doubled__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Resistance__ of a resistor is directly proportional to its length.
 
• When the length of the resistor is doubled, its resistance also doubles.
 
• The formula for resistance is R = ρ(L/A), where R is resistance, ρ is resistivity, L is length, and A is area.
 
• All other factors such as resistivity and cross-sectional area remain constant.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

 
• **Factors Affecting Resistance:**

 
 
• Resistance increases with an increase in the length of the conductor.
 
• Resistance decreases with an increase in the cross-sectional area of the conductor.
 
• Material resistivity plays a key role in determining resistance.
 
 
 
• **Applications of Resistance:**
 
 
• Used in electronic circuits to control current flow.
 
• Resistance helps in dissipating energy as heat in resistors.
